title: Higher Rates; Uneven Pain
text:
Higher Rates; Uneven Pain

Cedric Gemehl

Gavekal Research | 11 Sep 2026

The European Central Bank delivered a well-telegraphed 25bp rate hike on Thursday. At 2.5%, its policy rate is now at the upper bound of the 1.75% to 2.5% range the ECB’s most recent estimates suggest is neutral for the eurozone economy. Any further interest rate hikes will push monetary policy increasingly into restrictive territory. The question for investors therefore is no longer simply whether the ECB will hike again. It is also how much further hikes will put a brake on eurozone economic activity.ECB president Christine Lagarde took care to duck the first question during Thursday’s press conference. She repeated the ECB’s recent mantra that given the high level of uncertainty, policymakers will continue to take a meeting-by-meeting, data-dependent approach. However, several factors point to more ECB rate hikes in the near term.
